```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(haven)
library(knitr)

case31 <- read_sav("case31-prepped.sav")

fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), "--", ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", sprintf("%.3f", p))))
}

service_names <- c(
  "Regular share account", "Special subaccounts", "Christmas club account",
  "IRA", "Master credit card", "Signature loans", "New car loans",
  "Late model car loans", "Older model car loans", "Household goods loans",
  "Recreational loans", "Share collateralized loan", "IRA loans",
  "Line of credit loans"
)

residence <- factor(case31$q38, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Headquarters area", "Elsewhere"))
```

# R3: Employee proficiency

R3 asks: *What are members' attitudes and beliefs about the proficiency of credit union employees?*

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-descriptives
#| tbl-cap: "Employee proficiency composite"

r3_desc <- data.frame(
  N = sum(!is.na(case31$at_emp)),
  Mean = mean(case31$at_emp, na.rm = TRUE),
  SD = sd(case31$at_emp, na.rm = TRUE),
  Median = median(case31$at_emp, na.rm = TRUE),
  Minimum = min(case31$at_emp, na.rm = TRUE),
  Maximum = max(case31$at_emp, na.rm = TRUE)
)
kable(r3_desc, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-r3-histogram
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the employee-proficiency composite"

hist(
  case31$at_emp,
  breaks = seq(2.5, 5.25, by = 0.25),
  col = "#8ecae6",
  border = "white",
  main = "Attitude toward employee proficiency",
  xlab = "Mean of Q3--Q6"
)
abline(v = mean(case31$at_emp), col = "#d1495b", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
```

## One-sample t-test

The composite mean was compared with 4, the response value for **Agree**.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-ttest
#| tbl-cap: "One-sample t-test for employee proficiency (test value = 4)"

r3_test <- t.test(case31$at_emp, mu = 4)
r3_test_table <- data.frame(
  Mean = mean(case31$at_emp),
  `t value` = unname(r3_test$statistic),
  df = unname(r3_test$parameter),
  `p value` = r3_test$p.value,
  `95% CI lower` = r3_test$conf.int[1],
  `95% CI upper` = r3_test$conf.int[2],
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(r3_test_table, digits = 3)
```

## R3 insight

Members had a favorable view of employee proficiency. The average score was **4.21 out of 5**, slightly above the “Agree” point and statistically higher than 4 (*t*(127) = 3.91, *p* \< .001). Courteousness, helpfulness, professionalism, and availability were generally rated positively.

# R6: Operational effectiveness

R6 asks: *What are members' attitudes and beliefs about how effectively the credit union is operated?* The analysis includes statement frequency and accuracy (Q9--Q10), communication and confidentiality questions (Q11--Q12), four operational statements (Q31--Q34), and the overall rating (Q37).

## Metric-item descriptives and one-sample t-tests

For the metric items, the neutral or middle comparison value was 3. Because Q31--Q34 did not form a reliable one-dimensional scale in the previous activity, they are reported separately.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-metric
#| tbl-cap: "Operational-effectiveness ratings and one-sample t-tests (test value = 3)"

r6_metric_vars <- c("q10r", "q31", "q32", "q33", "q34", "q37r")
r6_metric_labels <- c(
  "Statement accuracy", "Financial information is confidential",
  "Loan processing is prompt", "CU meets members' needs",
  "Loan application is simple", "Overall CU rating"
)

r6_metric <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(r6_metric_vars), function(i) {
  x <- case31[[r6_metric_vars[i]]]
  tt <- t.test(x, mu = 3)
  data.frame(
    Measure = r6_metric_labels[i],
    N = sum(!is.na(x)),
    Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    t = unname(tt$statistic),
    df = unname(tt$parameter),
    p = ifelse(tt$p.value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", tt$p.value))
  )
}))
kable(r6_metric, digits = 2)
```

## Categorical-item frequencies

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-categorical
#| tbl-cap: "Response patterns for categorical operational items"

r6_cat <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    Measure = "Statement frequency",
    Response = c("Not often enough", "About right"),
    N = as.numeric(table(factor(case31$q9r, levels = c(2, 3)))),
    Percent = 100 * as.numeric(prop.table(table(factor(case31$q9r, levels = c(2, 3)))))
  ),
  data.frame(
    Measure = "Statements are easy to understand",
    Response = c("Yes", "No"),
    N = as.numeric(table(factor(case31$q11, levels = c(1, 2)))),
    Percent = 100 * as.numeric(prop.table(table(factor(case31$q11, levels = c(1, 2)))))
  ),
  data.frame(
    Measure = "Account confidentiality response",
    Response = c("Yes", "No", "Other / no opinion"),
    N = as.numeric(table(factor(case31$q12, levels = c(1, 2, 3)))),
    Percent = 100 * as.numeric(prop.table(table(factor(case31$q12, levels = c(1, 2, 3)))))
  )
)
kable(r6_cat, digits = 1)
```

The categorical response distributions were not equal across categories (all goodness-of-fit tests, *p* \< .001). The most visible pattern was that 77.3% viewed statement frequency as “about right,” and 97.7% said the statements were easy to understand.

## R6 insight

Overall, members viewed the credit union's operations favorably. The overall rating averaged **4.07 out of 5**. Among Q31--Q34, confidentiality received the highest mean (3.95), while loan-application simplicity received the lowest mean (3.46). All six metric means were above the comparison value of 3 (all *p* \< .001). The results are positive, but loan-application simplicity and promptness have more room for improvement than confidentiality.

# R4: Differences by residence

R4 asks whether members who live near the headquarters differ from members who live elsewhere in employee-proficiency attitudes, service awareness, and operational-effectiveness attitudes.

# R4a: Employee proficiency by residence

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a-descriptives
#| tbl-cap: "Employee-proficiency ratings by residence"

r4a_desc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(residence), function(g) {
  x <- case31$at_emp[residence == g]
  data.frame(
    Residence = g,
    N = sum(!is.na(x)),
    Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}))
kable(r4a_desc, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-r4a-boxplot
#| fig-cap: "Employee-proficiency ratings by residence"

boxplot(
  case31$at_emp ~ residence,
  col = c("#90be6d", "#f9c74f"),
  ylab = "Employee-proficiency composite",
  xlab = "Residence",
  main = "Employee proficiency by residence"
)
```

## Independent-samples t-test

The variance test was not significant (*F*(56, 70) = 0.90, *p* = .686), so equal variances were used for this comparison.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a-ttest
#| tbl-cap: "Independent-samples t-test for employee proficiency"

r4a_test <- t.test(case31$at_emp ~ residence, var.equal = TRUE)
r4a_table <- data.frame(
  `Mean difference` = unname(diff(r4a_test$estimate)),
  t = unname(r4a_test$statistic),
  df = unname(r4a_test$parameter),
  `p value` = r4a_test$p.value,
  `95% CI lower` = r4a_test$conf.int[1],
  `95% CI upper` = r4a_test$conf.int[2],
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(r4a_table, digits = 3)
```

## R4a insight

Headquarters-area members had a slightly higher mean (4.28) than members living elsewhere (4.14), but the difference was not statistically significant (*t*(126) = 1.29, *p* = .198). Therefore, perceptions of employee proficiency appear similar across the two residence groups.

# R4b: Service awareness by residence

## Cross-tabulations and chi-square independence tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-awareness
#| tbl-cap: "Service-awareness patterns and chi-square tests by residence"

awareness_vars <- paste0("q", 13:26, "r")

r4b_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(awareness_vars), function(i) {
  x <- case31[[awareness_vars[i]]]
  tab <- table(factor(x, levels = 1:3), factor(case31$q38, levels = 1:2))
  tab_test <- tab[rowSums(tab) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab_test))
  pct <- 100 * prop.table(tab, margin = 2)
  data.frame(
    Service = service_names[i],
    `HQ: unaware %` = pct[1, 1],
    `Elsewhere: unaware %` = pct[1, 2],
    `Chi-square` = unname(chi$statistic),
    df = unname(chi$parameter),
    p = ifelse(chi$p.value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", chi$p.value)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
kable(r4b_results, digits = 1)
```

## R4b insight

None of the 14 service-awareness measures had a significant association with residence (all *p* \> .05). For example, regular-share-account awareness did not differ by residence ($\chi^2$(2) = 1.27, *p* = .529). Although some percentages varied slightly, there was no consistent evidence that living near the headquarters improved awareness of available services.

# R4c: Operational effectiveness by residence

## Metric outcomes: two-group t-tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-metric
#| tbl-cap: "Operational-effectiveness means and tests by residence"

r4c_metric <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(r6_metric_vars), function(i) {
  x <- case31[[r6_metric_vars[i]]]
  tt <- t.test(x ~ residence)
  data.frame(
    Measure = r6_metric_labels[i],
    `HQ mean` = mean(x[residence == "Headquarters area"], na.rm = TRUE),
    `Elsewhere mean` = mean(x[residence == "Elsewhere"], na.rm = TRUE),
    t = unname(tt$statistic),
    df = unname(tt$parameter),
    p = ifelse(tt$p.value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", tt$p.value)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
kable(r4c_metric, digits = 2)
```

## Categorical outcomes: chi-square independence tests

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-categorical
#| tbl-cap: "Categorical operational measures and chi-square tests by residence"

r4c_cat_vars <- c("q9r", "q11", "q12")
r4c_cat_labels <- c("Statement frequency", "Statements easy to understand", "Account confidentiality response")

r4c_cat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(r4c_cat_vars), function(i) {
  tab <- table(case31[[r4c_cat_vars[i]]], case31$q38)
  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))
  data.frame(
    Measure = r4c_cat_labels[i],
    `Chi-square` = unname(chi$statistic),
    df = unname(chi$parameter),
    p = ifelse(chi$p.value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", chi$p.value)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
kable(r4c_cat, digits = 2)
```

## R4c insight

Most operational-effectiveness measures did not differ by residence. The one exception was loan-application simplicity: members living elsewhere rated applications more positively (3.61) than headquarters-area members (3.28), and this difference was significant (*t*(94.24) = -2.28, *p* = .025). The other metric and categorical comparisons were not significant. Since many tests were performed, this single difference should be interpreted carefully.

# Overall conclusion

Members generally rated employee proficiency and credit-union operations positively. Residence was not related to employee-proficiency ratings or service awareness, and nearly all operational measures were also similar between the groups. The main practical concern is loan-application simplicity, which received a lower overall rating and was rated especially low by headquarters-area members.
